title: PRD: Graceful structured response contracts for function-call escalation and stream recovery
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem statement: Customers integrating long-running structured streams with function/tool calls observe two classes of failures in production: (1) partial or malformed structured frames mid-stream (JSON schema drift, truncated fragments), and (2) non-deterministic duplicate or lost function invocations during retries and network interruptions. These lead to incorrect downstream state, difficult operator recovery, and customer-facing errors.

Goals:
- Define a pragmatic, testable acceptance contract for structured stream envelopes and function-call handoffs that minimizes silent data loss and supports deterministic operator recovery.
- Specify error modes, checkpointing semantics, idempotency primitives, and telemetry needed for incident triage and automatic rollbacks.
- Provide a rollout plan with gated experiments and e2e verification harnesses.

Non-goals:
- Not designing a new rich type system for application data (we'll rely on schema versions and simple typed envelopes).
- Not changing user-facing SDKs for non-streaming requests in this phase.

Key concepts (brief):
- Envelope: each emission in a stream is an envelope with headers + payload. Headers include seq_id, checkpoint_token (opaque), schema_version, and optional repair_hint.
- Checkpoint: server-generated token that represents a durable commit point; clients/operators can request replay/resume from a checkpoint.
- Call handshake: when model intends a function/tool call, it emits a call_frame that includes call_id, idempotency_key, expected_schema, and an estimated timeout.

Acceptance criteria (see separate list field for machine parsing) are the gates for Done. They are specific and testable.

Operator and SRE concerns: provide operator playbook snippets for manual resume, and ensure logs include call_id and checkpoint_token for every function-call transition.

Rollout: feature gated under flag "structured_stream_contract_v2"; start on a dedicated infra pool that supports deterministic replay.

Metrics (success):
- Reduction in incidents where stream-schema-truncation leads to failed downstream jobs by >= 75% in pilot tenants.
- Mean time to repair (operator-driven resume) < 15 minutes in simulated network partition tests.
- Zero duplicated effective side-effects for idempotent function calls across 10k simulated retries in harness.

References and artifacts: see artifact_links field.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope headers: every stream emission MUST include headers: seq_id (monotonic per connection), checkpoint_token (opaque, server-signed), schema_version (semver string), and optional repair_hint. Missing headers must cause runtime to tag the emission as 'header_incomplete' and route to degraded-path metrics.

Checkpointing: any emitted checkpoint_token must be persistently stored within the control plane before it is announced to the client; clients must be able to request resume-from(checkpoint_token) and receive a stream consistent with having consumed emissions up to that token.

Function-call handshake: a call_frame must include call_id, idempotency_key (client-supplied or generated by runtime), expected_schema, and terminal_statuses defined as one of: completed, failed, deferred, retried. The runtime must never emit more than one terminal_status for the same call_id unless a documented replay scenario occurs.

Idempotency and side-effects: if a function/tool declares idempotency_key, backend gateways must ensure at-most-once effective execution semantics for side-effecting actions across retries (simulated by test harness). For non-idempotent calls, runtime must mark calls as 'non-idempotent' and require explicit opt-in via route policy to allow retries.

Invalid fragment handling: when the runtime receives a malformed or truncated payload mid-stream, it must attempt up to 2 automated repairs using repair_hint; if repair fails, emit a 'partial' envelope that contains the latest valid checkpoint_token and a standardized error code (SRV_STREAM_PARTIAL_EMIT). The stream MUST remain open unless a terminal failure is explicitly signaled.

Backpressure and gateway behavior: when downstream capacity is exceeded, the gateway must return a STREAM_BACKPRESSURE frame with recommended_retry_after (ms) and an associated checkpoint_token. Clients must obey recommended_retry_after and use the checkpoint_token to resume without duplicating processed emissions.

Schema evolution guarantees: when schema_version increases incompatible-major, runtime must emit a schema_upgrade_notice envelope before the first emission using the new schema_version. Consumers may opt-in to strict mode, where a schema mismatch causes connection termination with a clear error code.

Observability contract: every call_frame, checkpoint_token issuance, and repair attempt must emit structured telemetry (call_id, seq_id, schema_version, repair_attempts, runtime_node) to the centralized tracing system within 30s of the event. Dashboards must display top-20 call failure reasons and aggregate mean repair_attempts per tenant.

E2E test pass criteria: end-to-end harness that simulates network drop, model mid-stream schema mutation, and duplicate function-call retries must show no more than 1% divergence in final reconstructed object across 1,000 runs per scenario; idempotent call tests must show zero duplicated side-effects across 10k simulated retries.

Operator resume flow: manual resume from a checkpoint via Console must replay emissions from checkpoint_token and provide a preview diff highlighting fields changed since token; resume action must be logged with operator identity and cause an audit event retained for 90 days.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope header validation and schema_version parsing in runtime (coverage >= 95% for header module)

Integration: simulate model emitting call_frame + truncated payload; verify auto-repair logic attempts 2 repairs, then emits partial envelope with SRV_STREAM_PARTIAL_EMIT and retains checkpoint_token.
Chaos: inject network partition between runtime and function-execution backend while forcing retries; verify at-most-once semantics for idempotent calls via test harness counters.
Load: baseline 1k concurrent streaming sessions with mix of small and large envelopes; measure checkpoint issuance latency p50/p95 and ensure < 50ms p50 on dedicated infra pool.
Operator UAT: Console resume workflow tested by SRE and Solution Engineers on staging with manual replay and audit log validation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): enable feature flag for internal Redwood tenants only on dedicated pool; run smoke tests and telemetry checks.
Phase 2 (pilot): opt-in for 5 pilot customers with high streaming usage; monitor incidents and MTTR for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to 25% of eligible production traffic with runtime-side soft-fail enabled; collect metrics and iterate on acceptance criteria.
Phase 4 (general availability): enable by default and publish public docs + migration guide.
